Cox model with provider strata or a pooled baseline

Source: R/model_cox.R
fit_cox.Rd

Fits the Cox proportional hazards model of the survival measures (SMR, SHR, STrR) through survival::coxph(). By default the provider is a stratification variable, so that each provider has its own baseline hazard and the covariate effects are estimated within providers (He and Schaubel 2015); the national baseline is then the Breslow estimator over every row with the fitted linear predictor as an offset. This is the two-stage model of the KECC measures: stage one estimates the covariate effects in the stratified model, stage two estimates the optional covariates x2 with the stage-one linear predictor as offset and gives the baseline. With strata = "none" one pooled model is fitted, without provider effects.

Usage

fit_cox(
  data,
  strata = c("provider", "none"),
  x2 = NULL,
  ties = c("breslow", "efron"),
  message = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

an object from pp_data() with a survival outcome (time, event, optional start, weights and offset).

strata

"provider" (default) or "none".

x2

optional names of covariate columns fitted in the second stage with the first-stage linear predictor as offset (calendar-year indicators in the KECC measures, say); they must be in data's covariates x or be further numeric columns of the original data frame named in x. NULL (default) for no second-stage covariates.

ties

"breslow" (default, the KECC convention) or "efron".

message

print the fit. Default FALSE.

Value

An object of class cox: a list with

coefficients

beta (first stage) and beta2 (second stage, or NULL).

stage1, stage2

the survival::coxph() fits (stage2 is NULL without x2).

linear_predictor

the full linear predictor of every included row, including the offset.

expected, residuals

expected events and martingale residuals per row.

baseline

a data frame with the distinct event times and the national cumulative baseline hazard.

data, vars, sizes, rows, control, converged

as in fit_logistic_fe().

Details

Rows with included = FALSE are left out; set cutoff = 0 in pp_data() to fit every provider, as the measures do, and choose the providers to report in test().

When data has a patient column it is passed as cluster to survival::coxph(), so that the robust (patient-clustered) covariance is available from vcov.cox() and summary().

The expected number of events of every row is \(E_i = \exp(\eta_i)\,[\Lambda_0(t_i) - \Lambda_0(s_i)]\) with \(\eta_i\) the full linear predictor (covariates of both stages and the offset) and \(\Lambda_0\) the Breslow estimator of the national cumulative baseline hazard at \(\eta = 0\), weighted by the case weights; the row's martingale residual is \(\delta_i - E_i\). For ties = "breslow" these are the residuals survival::residuals.coxph() returns for the second-stage model, and expected is what the KECC measures compute as event - residual.

References

He K, Schaubel DE (2015). Standardized mortality ratio for evaluating center-specific mortality: assessment and alternative. Statistics in Biosciences, 7, 296-321.

Liu D, Schaubel DE, Kalbfleisch JD (2012). Computationally efficient marginal models for clustered recurrent event data. Biometrics, 68(2), 637-647.

See also

standardize.cox(), test.cox(), summary.cox()

Examples

s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, type = "survival", seed = 1)
ps <- pp_data(s, x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", time = "stop", start = "start",
              event = "event", cutoff = 0, message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_cox(ps)
fit
#> Cox model stratified by provider (two-stage)
#>   2679 rows, 20 providers, 3 covariates; 336 events; ties breslow
#>   expected events sum to 336
coef(fit)$beta
#>         x1         x2         x3 
#>  0.5168166 -0.1163487  0.2665547
